_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from Synapse's documentation; no upstream egg.
name: Synapse
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Synapse is the reference Matrix homeserver, for chat that federates with the rest of Matrix. The egg runs it with SQLite for small servers, with sign-ups off and an admin account from its settings.
startup:
v=$(cat .synapse-version); want="$v $(python3 --version)"; if [ "$want" != "$(cat venv/.raptor-installed 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo "Installing Synapse $v"; rm -rf venv; python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir --disable-pip-version-check "matrix-synapse==$v" && echo "$want" > venv/.raptor-installed || { echo "Synapse $v couldn't be installed. Restart to try again."; exit 1; }; fi; printf 'listeners:
  - port: %s
    bind_addresses: ["0.0.0.0"]
    type: http
    tls: false
    x_forwarded: true
    resources:
      - names: [client, federation]
        compress: false
' {{SERVER_PORT}} > .raptor-listeners.yaml; c="-c homeserver.yaml -c .raptor-listeners.yaml"; [ -f data/signing.key ] || venv/bin/python -m synapse.app.homeserver $c --generate-keys || exit 1; if [ -n "{{ADMIN_USER}}" ] && [ -n "{{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}" ] && [ ! -f "data/.raptor-admin-{{ADMIN_USER}}" ]; then ( for i in $(seq 150); do sleep 2; curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:{{SERVER_PORT}}/health && break; done; r=$(venv/bin/register_new_matrix_user -c homeserver.yaml -u "{{ADMIN_USER}}" -p "{{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}" --admin http://127.0.0.1:{{SERVER_PORT}} 2>&1); case "$r" in *Success*|*"already taken"*) touch "data/.raptor-admin-{{ADMIN_USER}}"; echo "The admin account {{ADMIN_USER}} is ready." ;; *) echo "The admin account couldn't be made: $r" ;; esac ) & fi; exec venv/bin/python -m synapse.app.homeserver $c

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Synapse: checks the release exists and writes a first configuration
# (SQLite, sign-ups off, no usage stats). Synapse itself is installed from
# PyPI into the server's venv folder on the next start, by the server's
# Python. The database, media, signing key and homeserver.yaml are never
# touched once there.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag element-hq/synapse "$version") || exit 1
echo "${tag#v}" > .synapse-version

mkdir -p data/media_store
if [ ! -f homeserver.yaml ]; then
    name="${SYNAPSE_SERVER_NAME:-}"
    [ -n "$name" ] || fail "Set Server name (such as example.com), then reinstall: it's part of every user's ID and can't change later."
    secret() { openssl rand -hex 32; }
    cat > homeserver.yaml <<YAML
# Synapse's settings: https://element-hq.github.io/synapse/latest/usage/configuration/config_documentation.html
# Restart the server after changing this file. The listener (port and
# address) is written to .raptor-listeners.yaml at every start, from the
# server's settings: don't add listeners here.
server_name: "$name"
pid_file: /home/container/data/homeserver.pid
database:
  name: sqlite3
  args:
    database: /home/container/data/homeserver.db
media_store_path: /home/container/data/media_store
signing_key_path: /home/container/data/signing.key
# Sign-ups are off: the admin account comes from the server's settings,
# and more users can be made by an admin.
enable_registration: false
# No anonymous usage statistics sent to the Matrix developers.
report_stats: false
registration_shared_secret: "$(secret)"
macaroon_secret_key: "$(secret)"
form_secret: "$(secret)"
trusted_key_servers:
  - server_name: "matrix.org"
suppress_key_server_warning: true
YAML
    chmod 600 homeserver.yaml
    echo "Wrote a first configuration for $name."
fi
echo "Installed Synapse ${tag#v}; it's downloaded on the first start."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Synapse version to install, such as 1.165.0, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Server name
variables.description: The domain in your users' Matrix IDs, such as example.com for @alex:example.com. Set it before the first install: it can't change later.

variables.name: Admin username
variables.description: The admin account made on the first start, without the @ or the domain.

variables.name: Admin password
variables.description: The admin account's password, used when the account is made. Change it in your Matrix client afterwards.
